message.content:
# Evaluating ∫ 2·exp(x)·cos(x) dx

## Setting Up Integration by Parts

I'll first compute ∫ exp(x)·cos(x) dx, then multiply by 2.

Let **I** = ∫ exp(x)·cos(x) dx

**First integration by parts:** Choose u = cos(x), dv = exp(x) dx
- du = -sin(x) dx, v = exp(x)

$$I = \text{exp}(x)\cdot\cos(x) + \int \text{exp}(x)\cdot\sin(x)\, dx$$

**Second integration by parts** on ∫ exp(x)·sin(x) dx: Choose u = sin(x), dv = exp(x) dx
- du = cos(x) dx, v = exp(x)

$$\int \text{exp}(x)\cdot\sin(x)\, dx = \text{exp}(x)\cdot\sin(x) - \int \text{exp}(x)\cdot\cos(x)\, dx = \text{exp}(x)\cdot\sin(x) - I$$

## Solving for I

Substituting back:

$$I = \text{exp}(x)\cdot\cos(x) + \text{exp}(x)\cdot\sin(x) - I$$

$$2\cdot I = \text{exp}(x)\cdot\cos(x) + \text{exp}(x)\cdot\sin(x)$$

$$I = \frac{\text{exp}(x)\cdot(\cos(x) + \sin(x))}{2}$$

## Final Result

Multiplying by 2:

$$\int 2\cdot\text{exp}(x)\cdot\cos(x)\, dx = \text{exp}(x)\cdot\cos(x) + \text{exp}(x)\cdot\sin(x) + C$$

## Verification

Differentiating the result:
- d/dx [exp(x)·cos(x)] = exp(x)·cos(x) − exp(x)·sin(x)
- d/dx [exp(x)·sin(x)] = exp(x)·sin(x) + exp(x)·cos(x)

Sum = 2·exp(x)·cos(x) ✓

<answer>exp(x)*cos(x) + exp(x)*sin(x) + C</answer>

Then du = -sin(x) dx, v = exp(x)

u = sin(x), dv = exp(x) dx
du = cos(x) dx, v = exp(x)

∫ exp(x)*sin(x) dx = exp(x)*sin(x) - ∫ exp(x)*cos(x) dx
= exp(x)*sin(x) - I

So:

2*I = exp(x)*cos(x) + exp(x)*sin(x)
I = exp(x)*(cos(x) + sin(x)) / 2

Therefore:
∫ 2*exp(x)*cos(x) dx = 2 * I = exp(x)*(cos(x) + sin(x)) + C

= exp(x)*cos(x) + exp(x)*sin(x) - exp(x)*sin(x) + exp(x)*cos(x)
